name: AI Deep Dive — AMD — 2026-05-02
rationale: AMD has executed a remarkable turnaround — EPYC server CPUs now hold ~25% datacenter share and MI300 AI GPUs are generating $5B+ annually, driving 34% YoY revenue growth to $34.6B TTM with positive $6.7B FCF and improving 12.5% net margins. However, at $360 (32x forward P/E), the stock is pricing in continued strong execution that our probability-weighted DCF suggests is slightly ahead of fundamentals. Our weighted fair value of $320.12 implies 11% downside. AMD is a SELL — not because the company is failing, but because the current price leaves insufficient margin of safety given realistic scenario probabilities.

bear.rationale: Bear: AI GPU market growth decelerates and AMD fails to break CUDA's software moat. Revenue CAGR of 15% reflects deceleration from current 34% as the AI cycle normalizes and Intel EPYC competition re-intensifies. Net margin of 10% — BELOW TTM 12.52% — reflects increased R&D spend to compete with NVIDIA Blackwell successor (Rubin) without commensurate revenue share gains. ⚠️ NOTE: Prior Gemini analysis used 18% bear margin — a critical error since 18% > TTM 12.52%, meaning it modeled margin EXPANSION in the bear case. A bear case must reflect downside risk, not optimistic scenarios. Exit PE 18x is below semiconductor median (25x), appropriate for a company losing the AI GPU race. QM 0.90: competitive position weakening if EPYC gains stall. 1.5%/yr dilution from RSU grants with no buyback capacity.
risks: CUDA ecosystem lock-in proves insurmountable — NVIDIA maintains 85%+ AI training share as ROCm never closes the software gap; MI300X remains an inference-only niche
Intel 18A success + Arrow Lake recaptures x86 server CPU momentum, reversing AMD EPYC share gains — historical reference: Intel has reversed competitive deficits before (Sandy Bridge era 2011-2017)
AI capex cycle normalizes by 2027-2028; hyperscaler GPU spend decelerates sharply, commoditizing AMD's data center GPU revenue

base.rationale: No API analyst estimates available (yfinance returning empty estimates). Anchored to TTM YoY growth of 34.1%, applying deceleration: Y1 ~28%, Y2 ~24%, Y3 ~20%, Y4 ~18%, Y5 ~16% → 5-yr CAGR ~21-22%... adjusted to 28% to capture AI GPU ramp continuation. Note: no hypergrowth exception (34.1% < 40% threshold); growth within base case parameters. Net margin anchor: TTM 12.52% is the base (improving trend — see margin anchor note). Base 20% = +7.5pp improvement via data center product mix shift (MI300 higher ASP/margin than client GPU), operating leverage on fixed R&D. AMD's gross margin has steadily expanded (44.9% → 49.5%) — this provides confidence in the improvement path. Exit PE 28x = semiconductor median; appropriate for a consistently executing growth company with real AI GPU exposure. QM 1.0 = average quality; EPYC switching costs are real in enterprise but not across-cycle moat. No net dilution — buybacks offset RSU grants (AMD has been buying back stock).
risks: NVIDIA releases Rubin architecture (2026-2027) maintaining a 2-generation performance lead, limiting AMD MI-series to inference/cost-sensitive workloads
No analyst estimates available from API (new data sparseness); base growth anchored to TTM YoY 34.1% with natural deceleration — higher uncertainty than typical

bull.rationale: Catalyst: ROCm software ecosystem reaches parity with CUDA for AI inference workloads (Q3-Q4 2026 timeframe based on current roadmap trajectory), combined with MI400 launch winning at least 2 major hyperscaler training contracts from NVIDIA. EPYC Turin (Zen 5) extends server CPU leadership, crossing 35% market share. AMD's data center revenue mix reaches 60%+ of total, driving net margins toward 28% (fabless-optimized, comparable to Qualcomm's best quarters). Revenue CAGR of 38% represents AMD closing significant ground on NVIDIA in the $200B+ AI accelerator market. Exit PE 38x justified as AMD re-rates toward premium semiconductor multiple; QM 1.05 = limited emerging moat via ROCm ecosystem if parity is achieved. AMD returns 1%/yr to shareholders via buybacks as FCF expands.
risks: Valuation re-rates from 38x to 25x if NVIDIA releases a dominant Rubin architecture — bull requires AMD to sustain premium multiple AND capture AI share simultaneously
Revenue of $173B in Y5 would make AMD 2/3 the size of current NVIDIA — requires massive share capture across multiple markets simultaneously

aiThesis.rationale: AMD is an excellent company at a slightly stretched valuation. The bull case — ROCm software parity enabling AMD to capture AI training GPU market share from NVIDIA — is real but low-probability given CUDA's decade-long ecosystem moat. The base case of 28% CAGR and 20% margins by year 5 produces a fair value of $254 — 30% below the current price. Only the bull case justifies $360+, and at 25% probability weighting, it contributes $194 to our $320 weighted fair value. The critical error in the prior Gemini 3 Pro analysis was modeling an 18% net margin in the bear case — higher than AMD's current TTM margin — which made the bear scenario look like an acceptable outcome rather than actual downside risk. Correcting this, and normalizing the quality multipliers within documented rules, produces a SELL at -11%. AMD should be on a watchlist for re-entry below $280.

analyticsLog.shareCountMethod: shares_diluted = 1,630,338,779 per API. NI/EPS derived: $4.335B / $2.67 = 1.624B (0.4% discrepancy — within 15% threshold, no action). Used shares_diluted as primary.
analyticsLog.marginAnchor: Improving trend (mixed — FY2023 dip is an outlier). Historical: 5.6% (FY2022) → 3.77% (FY2023, PC crash/inventory) → 6.36% (FY2024) → 12.52% TTM. FY2023 is an identifiable cyclical outlier (PC market crash + inventory correction well-documented). Excluding outlier, trend is clearly upward. TTM 12.52% used as anchor. Base margin 20% = +7.5pp from TTM over 5 years, justified by: (1) gross margin improvement trend (44.9%→49.5%); (2) data center AI GPU revenue mix shift to higher-margin products; (3) operating leverage on fixed R&D base. Within spirit of trending margin rule.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: No API analyst estimates available. Used TTM YoY revenue growth of 34.1% as reference anchor. No hypergrowth exception (34.1% < 40% threshold). Base CAGR 28% represents modest deceleration from current pace, justified by AI GPU ramp continuation and EPYC server share gains. Bear 15% reflects cycle normalization scenario. Bull 38% requires AMD to close substantial ground on NVIDIA in AI training GPUs.
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Technology — Semiconductors: conservative P/E 15, median P/E 25, growth P/E 40. Net margin typical 15-30%, best-in-class 40%+ (fabless leaders). Bear exitPE 18x (28% below median — competitive challenge scenario). Base 28x (12% above median — consistent execution premium). Bull 38x (52% above median — near-parity with NVIDIA multiple if AI GPU thesis materializes).
dataQualityFlags: No API analyst estimates returned (yfinance estimates section empty for AMD — unusual for large-cap; may be API data gap). Growth anchored to TTM YoY 34.1% with internal deceleration model only.
FY2023 net margin 3.77% is a documented cyclical outlier (PC market crash + channel inventory correction) — excluded from margin trend analysis; TTM 12.52% used as anchor.
Historical_revenue array contains a leading zero (index 0) — likely FY2021 data unavailable in API; treated as missing data point. Used available 4 years: FY2022-TTM.

PRIOR ANALYSIS FLAW (Gemini 3 Pro): Bear case used 18% net margin > TTM 12.52% — modeled margin EXPANSION in the bear scenario, fundamentally incorrect. QM 1.2 on bull exceeds documented threshold for 'exceptional durable pricing power' (AMD does not qualify). These errors inflated prior FV from ~$320 to $443. All assumptions re-derived.

priorAnalysisReview.priceDelta: 0% — same day analysis; Gemini 3 Pro analysis done today, now replaced
priorAnalysisReview.assumptionAudit: Critical flaw: Bear case used 18% net margin when TTM was 12.52% — this models margin EXPANSION in the bear scenario, which is fundamentally wrong (bear must represent downside). This single error inflated the bear PV substantially. Bull QM 1.2 = 'exceptional durable pricing power across cycles' tier — AMD has a good competitive position but CUDA lock-in means NVIDIA holds that tier, not AMD. Base QM 1.1 lacks specific moat citation per skill protocol. Corrected: bear margin 10% (realistic downside), bull QM 1.05 (limited emerging moat), base QM 1.0 (average quality).
priorAnalysisReview.modelQualityFlag: UNVALIDATED — Gemini 3 Pro is in the flagged non-Sonnet list. All assumptions treated as unvalidated and re-derived from scratch.
priorAnalysisReview.thesisOutcome: Same day — no price change to evaluate. Prior BUY thesis replaced with SELL based on corrected assumptions.
priorAnalysisReview.fundamentalChanges: Same day analysis — no new fundamental data. Key change is analytical corrections: bear margin error fixed, QM values corrected, action flips BUY → SELL. AMD fundamentals are strong but stock is slightly overvalued at 32x forward P/E given realistic scenario probabilities.

analyticsLog.confidenceBreakdown: 0.65/1.0 — Base: 1.0. -0.12 no API analyst estimates (large-cap gap unusual — may affect growth anchoring accuracy). -0.10 wide scenario distribution ($40 bear vs $776 bull) reflects genuine uncertainty about AMD's AI GPU competitive position vs NVIDIA. -0.05 FY2023 margin outlier creates mean-reversion ambiguity. -0.05 prior Gemini analysis was flagged UNVALIDATED with demonstrated errors. +0.02 positive: strong FCF ($6.7B), improving gross margins (consistent 4yr trend), and EPYC/MI300 market validation. AMD is a high-quality company — uncertainty is about valuation at current price, not about business quality.
